description:
Lightweight dual-panel file explorer that looks identical on Windows, macOS and Linux

A lightweight dual-panel file explorer that looks and behaves the same on
Windows, macOS and Linux. It is a single statically linked executable written
entirely in Rust and draws its own UI - no Qt, WebView or Electron.

Features: tabs, inline tree, preview pane (text, images, archive listings,
WASM plugins), built-in terminal, batch rename, checksums, duplicate finder,
folder compare and sync, fast copy (CopyFileEx with parallel small files),
favorites, trash with restore. Settings live in %APPDATA%\nexa-dir, or next to
the executable in a data folder for portable use.

What's new in 0.30.2
Fixes since 0.30.1:
- macOS: copying or moving onto a volume that ran out of space (or hit another write error) never finished — the transfer stalled at high CPU and could only be cancelled. The error is now reported and the item fails like on other systems (GAP-049).
- macOS: application bundles (.app) showed "96 B" in the size column before their folder size was calculated. The cell now stays empty until the size is known, like a folder (GAP-050).
New setting:
- Appearance → "Keep the main window active while a dialog is open" (window.dialog_keeps_active, on by default). On keeps the current behavior: while one of Nexa Dir's own dialogs (modal or modeless) has focus, the main window keeps its focused transparency. Off treats the main window as inactive as soon as a dialog takes focus, so the unfocused transparency applies.
Behavior changes:
- Window transparency defaults: focused 0 % → 5 %, unfocused 20 % → 10 %. Values you already changed in settings are kept; only the defaults move.

Nexa Dir 0.30.2
Cross-platform lightweight dual-panel file explorer (successor of nexa-dir2; the same screen on Windows, macOS and Linux) — installers plus a Windows portable zip.

Every package also bundles nexa-copy, the command-line copy/move tool built on the same transfer engine (nexa-copy --help: --move --verify (also verifies cross-volume moves before the source is removed) --mirror --by-content --dry-run --include/--exclude --max-bps <rate> --journal <file>/--resume <file> --job <file.json> --progress --report <file>). MSI/pkg/deb/rpm put it on PATH; the portable zip (winget/choco) exposes it as a command alias.
The same engine is also bundled as a C library, ndir_xfer (ndir_xfer.dll next to the exe on Windows · Contents/Frameworks/libndir_xfer.dylib on macOS · /usr/lib/nexa-dir/libndir_xfer.so on Linux) with its header include/ndir_xfer.h: ndir_xfer_run(job_json, progress_cb, user, cancel) takes the same job JSON as nexa-copy --job and returns a report JSON (ndir_xfer_abi_version() = 1).
Verify downloads with sha256sums.txt. Uninstall: Windows Apps & features · macOS sudo "/Applications/Nexa Dir.app/Contents/Resources/uninstall.sh" · Linux dpkg -r nexa-dir / dnf remove nexa-dir.
User data (settings, sessions, favorites, rename presets) lives in the settings folder and is kept on uninstall. Settings from 0.22.0 and earlier (nexa-dir2) are imported once on first start.

Package managers
winget install SosomLab.NexaDir            # Windows MSI (replaces the 0.22.0 Inno installer)
winget install SosomLab.NexaDir.Portable   # Windows portable
choco  install nexa-dir                    # Windows MSI
choco  install nexa-dir.portable           # Windows portable
brew install --cask kiros33/tap/nexa-dir   # macOS (Universal pkg)
Linux (apt/rpm repository): https://pkg.sosomlab.com
The winget and Chocolatey commands work once the central reviews are through; nexa-dir-0.30.2-package-manifests.zip attached here is the exact submission.

Signing
Builds made without a code-signing key are flagged by macOS Gatekeeper and Windows SmartScreen (signed builds on request).
- macOS: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Nexa Dir.app" (the brew Cask does this for you)
- Windows: SmartScreen → "More info" → "Run anyway"
